blocks.x: How Applied AI & GenAI lands in Last-Mile & Urban Logistics — the constraints that shape the build, the gated delivery pattern, and the deltas we commit against your baseline.

Last mile is the costliest mile: route density, delivery promise, failed-delivery economics and urban access rules. Dynamic routing, fleet telemetry and micro-hub orchestration decide whether the final mile makes money.

items: Dynamic multi-stop routing exceeds solver time budgets.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Enterprise AI Strategy & Roadmapping, Generative AI Platform Engineering, Conversational AI & Digital Humans from the Applied AI & Generative AI tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Dynamic routing, Delivery promise management, Failed-delivery recovery) on Dataq Compass and Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus. Governance inherits the sector frame — Urban access/LEZ rules among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Voice and avatar interfaces that resolve, not deflect — with emotion-aware escalation and full auditability.

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Logistics & Supply Chain level this capability reads as: traffic, weather and history-driven ETA models per lane and mode (promise accuracy up; penalties down). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Every program of this type runs the same weekly rhythm, so your team can plan around it. Weeks 1–2 measure and sign the baseline with your team; nothing builds against an unsigned number. Weeks 3–8 prove the pattern on deliberately bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — under a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, closing with a measured delta against the baseline. Every gate is pass, stop or redirect, in writing.
